## Bug fixes
- **A receptor number could appear metres high over the sheet.** On a Mac, the Sheet preview and exported sheets could show one receptor's number again as a giant white figure somewhere on the map (for example a large "4" over a building). Receptor numbers are now drawn once, on their markers.

## New features
- **Recover Unsaved Work.** **File › Recover Unsaved Work…** brings back work that was never saved: an autosave you declined at start-up, or a project you closed with **Don't Save**. AURIS keeps the five most recent.
- **Project backups.** Each time a project is saved, the copy it replaces is kept on this Mac (the last five of each project, outside your project folder). **File › Show Project Backups** opens them. The copy from before a project was first saved in a newer AURIS is always kept, so an older AURIS can still open it.
- **Open a damaged project.** When a project will not open, AURIS offers **Open What Can Be Read**: damaged parts of the file are read as far as possible, objects that cannot be restored are left out one by one, and if needed whole optional sections (saved results, sheets, scenarios) are set aside, and you are told exactly what was left out. The file itself is not changed until you save, and the damaged copy is kept in the project backups.
- **Export Diagnostics.** **Help › Export Diagnostics…** saves a zip of AURIS's log, crash traces and settings (with keys and logos removed) to attach to a support request. AURIS now keeps a log in `~/Library/Logs/AURIS` and says so if it closed unexpectedly last time.
- **Copy and paste any objects, also between projects.** ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘V (or Edit › Copy, Cut, Paste) work on the selected sources, receptors, buildings, barriers, roads, berms and areas, with all their settings. Within a project they paste at the pointer; into another AURIS project they keep their coordinates. Receptors keep their building and stack when those are copied with them. Each paste is one undo step.
- **Snap to other objects while drawing.** Holding Shift while drawing an area source, car park, attenuation area, line source, berm or site outline now snaps to nearby corners, edge midpoints and edges of buildings, barriers, roads and areas (as the Building and Barrier tools did for buildings), and the snapped object is highlighted. Without a nearby object, Shift snaps to angles as before.
- **Type lengths while drawing.** While drawing a barrier, road, building or other shape, type a length and press Enter: the next point is placed exactly that far from the last one, towards the pointer. Press Enter again (or double-click) to finish.
- **Nudge with the arrow keys.** With objects selected, the arrow keys move them 0.1 m (1 m with Shift); each nudge can be undone.
- **Offset copies.** Right-click a barrier, berm, line source, road or railway and choose **Offset Copy…** to place a copy alongside it at a set distance (positive to the left of its drawn direction), with all its settings; for example a barrier 3 m from a road edge.
- **Project templates.** **File › Save as Template…** keeps a project's setup (time periods, compliance profile, calculation and assessment settings, plan and sheet styles, contour palettes, road defaults, source groups and schedules) without its objects, maps or results; **File › New from Template** starts a project from it.
- **One window and door Rw for a building.** Set **Windows and doors › Sound reduction Rw** once on a building and every emitting window or door pane assigned to it uses it. In a pane's Inspector the inherited value shows greyed in the Transmission loss field; type a value to give that pane its own, and clear it to go back to the building's (0 dB if the building has none). A single Rw applies to every band of a pane entered as a spectrum. Panes from earlier projects keep the values they have.
- **− and + keys on sound level and Rw fields.** Single-value indoor level and transmission loss fields step by 1 dB, starting from the inherited value when the field is empty.
- **Façade receptors along a whole wall.** A building's **Facade receptors › Spacing along wall** places a receptor stack every so many metres along each wall (centred, so both ends are covered) instead of one in the middle. Leave it empty for one per wall, as before.
- **GeoJSON and CSV.** **File › Import CAD / GIS Layers** now also reads GeoJSON (with the `layer` property as layers, WGS84 or a named coordinate system) and CSV points (X/Y, Easting/Northing or Lat/Lon columns; every other column can be used as name or height), for example a receptor schedule from a spreadsheet. Export also writes GeoJSON.
- **BS 5228 construction noise assessment (ABC method).** Results has a **BS 5228** mode: enter the measured ambient LAeq for a period (or per receptor: double-click the cell, or paste a column from a spreadsheet), and each receptor shows its Table E.1 category and threshold, the margin and whether the effect is significant. Daytime, evening-and-weekend and night thresholds are chosen from the period's name and can be set per period; where the ambient already exceeds Category C, the 3 dB rule of note 2 applies. The Report pack workbook includes the assessment and its basis.
- **ProPG Stage 1 risk palettes.** Two new contour colour palettes show the ProPG: Planning & Noise initial site noise risk, by day (LAeq,16h: negligible below 50 dB to high from 70 dB) and at night (LAeq,8h: 40 to 60 dB), with the risk named in the sheet's legend.
- **DMRB LA 111 magnitude-of-change maps.** A difference map can be coloured by the DMRB LA 111 magnitude of change in road traffic noise, short term (negligible, minor from 1 dB, moderate from 3 dB, major from 5 dB) or long term (3, 5 and 10 dB), for increases and decreases, with the category named in the legend.
- **PDF sheets on A3, A2 and A1.** Choose the paper in the export dialog's format list (**PDF Document, A3** and so on); the sheet keeps its layout and scales with the page, and the choice is remembered for that sheet. The **Report pack** now also writes every sheet into one PDF, **All sheets.pdf**, each page on its sheet's paper size.

## Changes
- **Day, evening and night are calculated together.** Propagation does not change between periods, only the sources' levels do, so each source-to-receptor path is now solved once and reused for every period, with identical results: a three-period receptor run with lines and roads took 5 s instead of 18 s.
- **Large models no longer run out of memory.** A 1,000-building model with 20 roads used over 9 GB while calculating receptors (enough to stall a Mac); it now peaks at 4 GB, with the same levels. Building the visibility between obstacles for lateral paths is twice as fast on such models.
- **Small and medium receptor calculations are several times faster.** Calculations run inside the window were collecting profiling detail for every source-receiver path, which kept them off the compiled solver. They no longer do; results are identical (62 validation scenarios: 10 s to 1.5 s).
- **The plan is smoother on large models.** On a 5,000-building model, the pointer's hover and pick work takes 5 ms instead of 11 ms (picking a building edge 2 ms instead of 35 ms), and a zoomed-out redraw takes half as long (0.09 s instead of 0.18 s), so panning, zooming and hovering stay fluid.
- **The 3D view opens faster on large models.** Building foundations now sample the ground in one batch instead of point by point, and only the map tiles that hold pavement are cut around roads: a 1,000-building model with 20 roads and 1,000 receptors opens in 3D in 6.8 s instead of 13.9 s, and receptor and source markers are built twenty times faster. Editing one building rebuilds only that building's 3D shape (three times faster on 1,000 buildings).
- **Up to 10,000 sources, receptors, line sources and area sources of each kind** (was 512), for façade receptor grids and imported models.
- **SmartSmooth's Simplify keeps contours in place.** Simplify allowed each level to change by up to its dB tolerance, which in a weak far-field gradient let a line drift several metres (up to 3.9 m at the strongest setting on a test site). Now an even slope keeps its contours within a fraction of a grid cell, while bumps, dips and grid-scale wiggles are still smoothed away by the full tolerance. Against exact 0.25 m contours, lines are about twice as close at every Simplify and Smoothing setting (for example Simplify 4: 1.1 m instead of 2.4 m at the 95th percentile) and as smooth as before.
- **Smaller field steps are drawn as clean lines.** Calculate looked only for level steps of 0.3 dB or more. A smaller step matters when the level around it changes slowly (0.1 dB in a 0.1 dB/m far field moves a contour by a metre), and those are now found and proved too, down to 0.08 dB, so they no longer kink the contours.
- **Exported contours match the drawing.** GIS export (DXF, GeoPackage, Shapefile) now writes the contour lines the sheet shows (SmartSmooth, with its field-step lines), and a new **Contour bands** layer of filled band polygons with their range and label. Before, the lines were traced again from the raw grid, so they differed from the sheet and showed false rings around buildings.
- **Difference maps: more steps and an outlier-proof range.** Difference colour bands can be 0.5, 1, 2, 3 or 5 dB wide. **Ignore outliers** sets the range from 99 % of the map, so one extreme value (beside a new barrier, say) no longer washes the small changes that matter out to near-white; the few values beyond it show in the end colours, and the panel says how much of the map that is.
- **Shift-click selects several window panes.** Shift-clicking a pane now adds it to or removes it from the selection, so a row of windows can be edited together in the Inspector. Before, Shift on a selected pane toggled one of its end nodes, and Shift-clicking a pane already selected selected the building behind it instead.
- **Shift-snapping a receptor follows the building you point at.** The ghost stays on the façade of the building under the cursor, and switches to the next building only when the cursor crosses the line between them; before, the nearest wall of any building won, so on a shared wall it could jump to the neighbour. Walls wholly shared with an equally tall neighbour are no longer offered as façades. Snapping is also quicker on large models.
- **Receptors above a lower roof start above it.** A receptor Shift-placed on a wall over a lower adjoining building (a conservatory, a single-storey extension) starts 1.5 m above that roof instead of inside it, skips the floors below, and is labelled with the floor it is on (for example Fl. 1 above a 3 m roof). The status bar says what was done; change the floor in the Inspector if needed.
- **Façade receptors above a lower neighbour** (Place façade receptors) start 1.5 m above its roof, and the party-wall check is made at each stack instead of only at the middle of the wall.
- **Autosave is per window and reports problems.** Each running AURIS keeps its own autosave, so two windows never overwrite each other's recovery data, and a window that is still open is never offered as a crash to recover. If autosave fails twice in a row, the status bar says so instead of failing silently.
- **Settings are saved safely.** Settings are written in one step with the previous copy kept, so a crash while saving can no longer reset every preference and the recent-projects list. A damaged settings file falls back to that copy. The company logo is stored once instead of twice (3 MB less to read each time a project opens).

## Bug fixes
- **A source cutoff distance could drop a source that mattered.** With a cutoff set, contours checked each source against only a sample of the grid's points, so a source near an unsampled point could be left out entirely there. The cutoff is now measured against every point.
- **Declining crash recovery deleted the unsaved work.** Choosing **Open without restore** opened the last saved file and, in doing so, deleted the autosave the dialog said it would keep. Declined recovery data is now set aside in Recover Unsaved Work…, never deleted.
- **"Don't Save" before opening another project lost the work**, although the prompt said an autosave would be kept. It is now kept in Recover Unsaved Work….
- **File › New replaced unsaved work without asking**, and the autosave of that work was then cleared. It now asks to save first, as Open does.
- **Some plan edits could not be undone.** Flip, Union and Subtract of buildings, Paste building, and placing façade receptors (from the context menu or Auto-place) now each make one undo step; before, Cmd+Z skipped them or undid them together with an unrelated earlier edit.
- **Redo straight after Undo could do nothing** when the undone change had been typed in the Inspector: the field still held the typed value and Redo saved it again as a new edit, which cleared the redo history. The Inspector now shows the restored value as soon as you undo.
- **A calculation could wait forever if one of its processes was stopped** (for example by macOS when memory ran out). AURIS now notices, stops the calculation and says "A calculation process stopped unexpectedly (out of memory?)" instead of showing progress that never moves.
- **Receptor calculations kept running after AURIS closed unexpectedly**, using every core until they finished. They now stop with the window that started them.
- **A calculation could hang on a receptor or source with a coordinate that is not a number**, using all memory; it now stops with a message pointing to Model preflight.
- **One receptor outside CRTN's scope stopped the whole road calculation.** A receptor CRTN cannot assess on its own (terrain not covering its path, for example) now has no level and is listed under the results with the reason, and every other receptor is calculated. When no receptor can be assessed (traffic outside CRTN's range), the calculation still stops and explains why.
- **Roads and receptors left out of a calculation are reported.** A road whose emission could not be worked out, or receptors that could not be calculated, were skipped without a word. They are now listed under the results, in the report text and in the saved run.
- **Gaps in LiDAR terrain became 0 m**, making deep false pits (and false screening at their rims) on terrain given above sea level. Missing heights now take the nearest valid height.
- **An error inside a calculation could be shown as a cancellation** when its message happened to contain the word "cancel", and an error while checking for cancellation was ignored. Cancellation is now recognised as such and every other error is reported.
- **Buildings with impossible geometry are reported before calculating:** a height that is not a positive number stops the calculation with the building named, and footprints with no area are flagged as a warning (an outline that crosses itself is already listed by Model preflight).
- **Large models built slowly.** Adding each object rescanned every existing one, so building or importing 10,000 buildings took nearly a minute; it now takes a fraction of a second.
- **The 3D view could fall back to plain blocks on dense road networks** when road markings met nearly coincident edges at crossings; markings there are now worked out robustly. A road that is refused (for example over the object limit) no longer leaves a half-added road behind.
- **Restarting the 3D view could close AURIS** when the 3D renderer failed to start again. The 3D tab now shows why and lets you try again. When the full scene cannot be built and the view falls back to simple blocks, the status bar now says so instead of changing silently.
- **The menus stayed live during a long export or render.** While the Report pack, Every result, an Ultra render or a video was being made, menu commands (Open, New, Undo…) could still change the project underneath it. These now hold the whole app until they finish or are stopped.
- **Old caches and update installers piled up.** Font caches from every earlier version and installers of updates already applied are now removed after 14 days, in the background.

## New features
- **Export a video of the 3D view.** **Render → Export video…** makes an MP4 of the current view, ready for a presentation or a planning committee:
  - **Orbit**: circles the point the view looks at, at the same height and distance. A full turn loops seamlessly; a half or quarter turn swings either side of the view and eases in and out. Choose which way it turns.
  - **Fly-in**: sweeps in from high and wide and settles on the view.
  - **Sun study**: holds the view from sunrise to sunset over the site, on the day set in Lighting, so the shadows move round the buildings. The clock time is shown in the corner.
  - 720p, 1080p or 4K at 30 frames a second, from 3 to 60 seconds long. **Live** quality records the 3D view as you see it, about as fast as it plays. **Ultra** path traces every frame as the Ultra render, in the chosen render look; it takes much longer. The popover shows how long the video will take to make. Selection outlines and other editing cues are left out, and the view goes back to where it was afterwards.

## Changes
- **SmartSmooth's Simplify and Smoothing sliders respond at once.** After a calculation, every slider position is prepared in the background (in about 20 seconds for a typical sheet, nearest positions first), so moving a slider swaps in the finished drawing in a fraction of a second instead of rebuilding it for several seconds each time. Rebuilding a position not yet prepared is also about twice as fast.
- **Basemap brightness, and smoother basemap controls.** Each basemap layer has a Brightness slider beside Opacity and Contrast, in the editor and on sheets and exports. The map now follows the sliders as you drag instead of updating when you let go. The style popover is tidier: aligned rows, the map's name at the top, a proper Colour / Black & white switch, double-click a slider to reset it, and Reset is available only when something has changed.
- **SmartSmooth contours no longer scallop along shadow edges.** Where a building corner starts to screen a source, or a reflection appears, the calculated level steps by up to several dB across a line only a few centimetres wide. With area sources (such as façade windows), line sources or roads these lines were not known to the drawing, so the bands were interpolated across the step between grid points and came out wavy, scalloped and stair-stepped along every shadow ray. Calculate now finds these steps in the result, proves each one with extra exact receivers on both sides and places it to a few centimetres; SmartSmooth then draws it as one clean line, with each side's contours meeting it. Receiver values are never changed. This adds some seconds to a calculation (about 30 s for a busy façade scene).
- **Building names are always legible, in a colour that matches the building.** Labels on the plan, sheets and exports now take a darker shade of the building's outline (a lighter one on dark fills), deepened as far as needed to read clearly against the fill, instead of one fixed colour. The building style picker has a **Text** colour for setting your own, saved with presets, and a link to go back to following the outline. Three new presets: Slate, Warm grey and Print mono.
- **Ultra renders keep the map's own colours.** With a low sun most of the light comes from the blue sky, and the whole render (white buildings, the basemap's greens and greys) took on a lilac-blue cast. The render now balances the light's colour from the scene itself, measured with the surface colours taken out, so it does not depend on the map. Sunlit walls keep some warmth and shadows stay a cool blue-grey. The brightest sunlit walls also no longer burn out to flat white. This applies to the refined Ultra view too.
- **The 3D view's depth of field follows the render look.** Turning on **Depth of field** or **Tilt-shift** in **Render → Render look…** now blurs the live view the same way as the Ultra render, with the same lens; before, the live view's blur was barely visible. Tilt-shift shows in the live view as strong depth of field around the target; the tilted band of focus is in the Ultra render. The separate **Depth of field** checkbox in Lighting is replaced by a link to the render look.
- **The refined Ultra view updates faster.** Each refined image is finished in about 40 % less time (0.44 s instead of 0.74 s at full window size), so it sharpens more smoothly while you look.

## Bug fixes
- **Numbers on receptor markers and other labels could show holes** where a character's strokes cross (the 4 in particular). Lettering now keeps overlapping strokes.
- **AURIS could fill the disk with temporary calculation files.** Each calculation's worker processes kept a copy of the scene (tens of megabytes) for every batch of receivers until the calculation ended, and copies left by a crash or force-quit were never removed. Only the copies in use are kept now, and leftovers are removed when AURIS starts.
- **Contours could fail with "Failed in nopython mode pipeline … Known signatures".** Two things combined. After an update the app restarted with the previous version's settings for its calculation kernels, so every version since 0.41 kept using the 0.41 kernel folder: its own ready-compiled kernels were never installed, and each calculation compiled them again in all its worker processes at once. Workers compiling the same kernel at the same moment could then file one variant under another's name, and a later calculation picked up the wrong one and stopped. Each version now always uses its own kernel folder, and workers that compile at the same time no longer overwrite each other. First calculations after an update are also faster again, because the bundled kernels are used.
- **A crash when the main window's title bar was updated without the native Mac window system**, for example while the app was checked automatically without a display. The title bar now looks up the Mac window only on macOS's own window system.

## New features
- **The Ultra view refines itself when you stop moving.** In Ultra quality, a second or so after the camera stops, the view is path traced in the background and fades into the same image the Ultra render would save: a first image in under a second, clean within about 20 seconds. Moving the camera, editing or changing the lighting returns to the live view at once. Turn it off in **Render → Render look…**.
- **Render look.** **Render → Render look…** chooses how the Ultra render and the refined Ultra view look: **Natural**, **Clean** (for technical figures), **Cinematic** or **Miniature**. You can then fine-tune them:
  - **Depth of field** that really works: a lens focused on the point the view orbits, with the foreground and the distance out of focus.
  - **Tilt-shift**: a narrow band of focus through that point and strong blur above and below, so the site looks like a scale model. You can turn the band to follow a road.
  - **Glow** round sources and receivers, **grain**, **vignette** and **exposure**.
  - Your choice is remembered on this Mac.
- **Sources and receivers glow.** In the Ultra render each point source and receiver casts a soft light of its own colour onto the walls and ground beside it, with a faint halo. In the live view they light a small pool round themselves.

## Changes
- **Receivers are a deep, strong blue in 3D, as in the Ultra view**, and sources a strong red. They are drawn in their own colour in the Ultra render too, where the sky's lavender cast used to make receivers pale violet.
- **Imported maps are sharper.** OS and Google maps keep nearly all the detail of the tiles they are made from (0.10 m per pixel; it was 0.15 m per pixel, from the same tiles and the same number of requests). Re-import a map to get the sharper image. In 3D the map is now draped at up to 8,192 pixels across (it was 4,096), and filtered more finely at low viewing angles, so its lettering stays legible close up.
- **SmartSmooth contours no longer kink where they meet a building.** Contour lines now slide along walls and transition lines while they are smoothed, rather than being pinned beside them. Hairline strips and crumbs along walls join the band they belong to. On P1999 at Simplify 3 and 100 % smoothing, 90 sharp corners became 2 and 28 slivers became 2 (P2003: 34 to 4, P1922: 35 to 2, P2006: 25 to 0). The bands agree with the unsmoothed field as closely as before, to within 0.1 % of points.
- **Ultra renders finish faster.** The denoiser is compiled: about 5 seconds less at the end of every render.

## Bug fixes
- **Exported images and Ultra renders showed the teal selection outline** (and hover, pane handles). Exports and renders now leave out these editing cues; the 3D editor still shows them.

## Changes
- **Report-quality contours near buildings and barriers are up to twice as fast, with identical results.** Finding where screening changes along the contours ran thousands of small path checks one after another. They now run on all processor cores. P1988 takes 47 s instead of 106 s, and P1995 114 s instead of about 150 s. On six projects checked, the contours are unchanged.

## Changes
- **Contours next to façade-mounted and directional sources are far faster, with identical results.** For every piece of such a source, AURIS checked every building to see whether the source was mounted on it. It now checks only the buildings within the 5 cm mounting stand-off. P1922's report-quality contours take 16 s instead of 4.6 minutes, and P2003's receptors 4 s instead of 50 s.
- **Area sources behind thin walls calculate twice as fast.** A glass court wall modelled as 2 cm thick panels cut the area source along both faces of every panel, and again at every step in the wall's height, into slivers a few centimetres wide. Cuts closer than 3 cm now merge into one. P2003's full site at 1 m takes 61 s instead of 120 s. The integration is as accurate as before: against a four-times finer integration, the error is 0.03 dB RMS. Receptor levels on P2003 change by up to 0.1 dB, and on P2001 by 0.0001 dB; other projects are unchanged.
- **SmartSmooth no longer prepares the Interpolated Raster field.** Every calculation built the field the raster views draw from, although SmartSmooth doesn't use it. This took 1 to 15 s. Report-quality contours are now 1 to 16 s faster (P1998 50 s instead of 66 s, P1984 6 s instead of 13 s), with identical contours. Interpolated Raster and Gradient build that field when you switch to them, or during the calculation if one of them is selected.
- **CRTN calculations on a sloping site are 39% faster, with identical results.** On a terrain plane, each road segment's ground profile is now calculated in compiled code.

## Bug fixes
- **Report-quality contours failed with "Nonfinite exact propagation-region support" on P2000.** A CRTN road with fewer than 1,000 vehicles in 18 hours needs measurement (paragraph 30), so CRTN gives no level at some points. These points are now left as gaps, as the grid already shows them, instead of stopping the calculation.
- **Report-quality contours failed with "Continuous face has insufficient acoustic support" on one P1991 file.** A sliver region of 2×10⁻¹⁵ m², left by rounding, stopped the map. Regions that small are now ignored.

## Changes
- **The first calculation after an update is no longer slow.** AURIS used to compile its calculation code on the first calculation after every update, which on P2003 took 202 s instead of 113 s. The calculation code now comes ready-compiled inside the app.
- **Old calculation caches are cleared.** Each version left about 34 MB behind. Caches no installed copy of AURIS uses are now deleted, and one still used by another installed copy is kept.

## Changes
- **Report-quality contours are 3 to 7 times faster.** Refining a grid now stops at cells a quarter of the grid spacing across (at most 1 m), instead of chasing detail down to 6 cm. Against exact levels at 1,500 random points per site, the drawn bands are just as accurate as before, and more accurate than an exact grid at 1 m. On a 4 m grid, P2003 now refines in 67 s instead of 8 minutes, and P1922 in 4.4 minutes instead of 13.
- **ISO 9613-2 calculations use 11 to 23% less processor time, with identical results.** The most gain is around reflecting buildings and barriers. P2003's full site at 1 m now takes 120 s instead of 132 s.

## Changes
- **SmartSmooth, rebuilt from the ground up.** Contours are drawn by a new engine, with reflections on or off, in plan and in section:
  - **Simplify now states its accuracy.** Each step allows the drawn field to differ from the calculated levels by at most 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 dB (Raw: none). Within that, it draws the smoothest contours possible. Features smaller than the allowance (spikes, needles, notches, stair-steps) go, and anything larger is kept.
  - **No more hairs or needles.** Simplify also sets the narrowest feature it keeps (up to 1.5 grid cells). A path switching on and off over a few centimetres, such as a reflection at a façade corner, is no longer drawn as a needle or a hairy edge. Raw still shows it.
  - **Smoothing follows the contours.** Close to a source, where contours are tight, smoothing reaches only a short way and they keep their shape. Far afield, where contours are wide apart, it reaches further, giving long, clean curves.
  - **Smooth curves, never stair-steps.** The calculated grid is interpolated with a smooth curve that never goes beyond its neighbouring points, and simplified contour lines lose the grid's stair-steps.
  - **Walls and barriers are exact.** Contours never pass through a building, barrier or court wall. Where the level jumps across a wall, the bands on each side run straight up to it, with no slivers or specks along the wall.
  - **Bands and lines always agree.** Every band boundary is a single shared line: no gaps, overlaps or crossings at any setting.
  - **Faster.** A style change on a large site takes about a second.
- **Building labels on the map show just the house number** when the building is named by its address ("160 Camden High Street" shows as "160"). The full name stays in the Inspector and in exports.
- **Calculations are slightly faster** (about 3% on area-source contour maps), with identical results.

## Bug fixes
- **SmartSmooth painted some areas in the wrong band.** On a section behind a tall building, the area beyond the roof was drawn as 15–20 dB where the calculated levels are 9–15 dB.
- **SmartSmooth on Simplify Extreme kept thin needles and spikes**, and showed notches and stair-stepped edges near buildings and where reflections switch on or off.

## Bug fixes
- **Contour maps had empty squares along the line of a façade source's wall.** Grid points that fell on the wall's line, beyond the building's end or past the source, received no sound at all, so the basemap showed through. They now have their proper level.
- **Too little sound round the corner of a building from a façade source.** The path round the corner of the source's own building was left out, so levels just behind the façade's line, beside the building, dropped by about 30 dB instead of a few dB. Recalculate contour maps and receptors that include façade sources.
- **Façade sources disappeared from contour sheets** when contours were shown: they were drawn under the contour colours. They now draw on top, like point sources.

## Changes
- **Edit façade panes directly in 3D.** Click a vertical area source (a window, louvre or door on a façade) and:
  - **Drag it** to slide it along its façade, or drag its top, bottom or ends to resize it. The cursor and a teal edge show what a drag will do. Panes snap to the ground, the roof line, the ends of the façade and the edges of neighbouring panes, otherwise to 5 cm, and never slip off their façade or below ground.
  - **Hold ⌥ and drag** to copy it (works for any area source).
  - In **Properties › Façade pane**, set the bottom height above ground, the pane height and its width, or click **Duplicate** to place a copy beside it.
  - **Array…** repeats it across or up the façade: choose the direction (right, left, up, down, or a grid), how many across and up, and the gap or centre-to-centre spacing. A preview shows the new panes on the façade before you create them; copies that would leave the façade or land on an existing pane are left out and listed.
- **Place search finds places anywhere.** Northern Ireland, Ireland, the rest of Europe and beyond now come up alongside Ordnance Survey's Great Britain results, with each place's region and country shown.
- **CRTN road calculations near many buildings are about 15% faster**, with identical results.

## Bug fixes
- **Searching for a place in Northern Ireland found nothing** when an Ordnance Survey key was set (Ordnance Survey covers Great Britain only).

## Changes
- **Calculations are much faster on most sites, with identical results.** Every grid level matches 0.42 exactly; the time saved comes from doing the same calculation with less work. Measured on the test sites and your projects (CPU time per grid point):
  - Padel courts: P2001 Dragon Padel about **6×** faster (a 31 s grid now takes 4.4 s); courts with glass rebound walls about 1.5×; P2003 about 1.3×.
  - ISO 9613-2 roads near many buildings about **4×** faster; line sources about 2×.

- **Recovering unsaved work.** The recovery window is the only thing on screen while it is open; a large autosave shows its real contents (it read "No objects yet"), and Open last saved now opens the saved file.
- **The contour progress bar no longer stops at 0%** when a contour display update from before finishes after Calculate has started.
- **The railway Inspector no longer clips its right edge.**

## New features
- **Outline tool for site boundaries and mark-up.** A pen tool in the Editor toolbar (O) draws named outlines: the first is the red Site Boundary, and each new one takes the next free plan colour (cyan, blue, magenta, green, orange, purple, black) with a matching name. Select an outline to rename it, choose its colour (colours already used are unavailable), line style (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot), width, an optional soft halo, and whether its name is written along the line, with the line broken around the text. Corners are edited like buildings. Outlines draw above contours, stay visible in Map only, and appear in the contour sheet key under their own names. Red and blue lines from earlier versions become Site Boundary and Other land outlines.
- **One click to bring results up to date.** When a project opens with receptor levels or contours that no longer match the model, a quiet "Results out of date · Update" chip appears in the status bar. Clicking it recalculates receptor levels and then the contour grid.
- **Save without a dialog, and project folders.** Save on a new project writes it straight to the AURIS Projects folder, named from its number and name. Settings › General can switch this to asking each time, and Project folders adds folders (such as a company Projects share) that File › Open searches, with all their sub-folders.
- **Building numbers with their road.** Imported buildings tagged with only a house number take the nearest named road, so they arrive as "12 Kingfisher Way" instead of a generated id.

## Changes
- **A calmer start, and an Inspector that moves smoothly.** On a new project the Inspector stays tucked away behind the start card; Start drawing (or opening a project) glides it in on the Project tab, and Import a map reveals it once the import window has closed. Opening and closing the Inspector (double-click the handle, or View › Show/Hide Inspector) slides it in and out with easing. Dragging the handle moves the panel with a little weight, gives gently at its narrowest and widest, and a firm pull closes or opens it.
- **Map import window.** The map image now matches the map being viewed (Google, or OS mapping for OS and OpenStreetMap views), and a second image defaults to a different source. Floating cards have a soft shade and no outlines, and the layer card shows only what applies: a second map is one link away, and terrain detail, object types and the OS allowance appear only when relevant.
- **Model Preflight redesigned.** A plain headline says whether the model is ready, and findings are grouped as Must fix, Check, Review and Notes, each naming its object and offering its own fix.
- **Inspector refinement.** Sections align with the shared Identity and Geometry blocks, derived values read as plain text, and data tables lose their borders and grid. Buildings group their roof options into one row and show parapet height only when the parapet is on; hand-entered sources leave out library rows they cannot use; receptors show their latest saved level instead of "No calculated level yet".
- **Project panel.** Dated notes show the date, time and consultant (with titles) as a quiet heading so the note leads; choosing calculation periods applies them at once; section headings align with their captions.
- **Progress bars ease to a stop.** Stopping slows and fades the shimmer instead of freezing it, the status bar progress fades out, and start-up progress decelerates if start-up pauses.
- **Level bars ease in** when Results shows new levels.
- **Editor layout.** One gutter either side of the canvas; the collapsed Inspector handle sits centred against the window edge. The model check's warning mark has rounder corners.
- **Faster SmartSmooth on large refined areas.** Cells with nothing to refine are meshed in one batch even where the area has refinement elsewhere (P1963: 27 s to 25 s).
- **Faster CRTN road contours.** Each receiver's terrain-screening check reads its ground profile in one pass and reuses path sections (P1961: 39.5 s to 28.8 s per 200 receivers), and building screening tests every building's extent at once before forming sections (P1987: 23.3 s to 18.5 s per 60 receivers). Levels are identical.
- **Tighter Inputs and Results tables.** Inputs sizes summaries to their content, drops grid lines and mutes names that only repeat the ID. Results hides the Sound field column on screen when every receptor uses the method's convention (exports keep it).

## Bug fixes
- **Inputs shows receptor levels.** Receptor rows always said "not calculated"; they now show the scenario's latest level for the period (the range across a stack's floors), marked when the model has changed since.
- **Calculate explains a model with every source switched off.** When every source and road was disabled, contours used to run and then fail with "Nonfinite exact propagation-region support". Calculate now says that everything is switched off and how to turn a source back on.
- **The road Inspector no longer clips its right edge.**
- **Long project names stay on one line** in the window title after leaving full screen.
- **Alt-click adds and removes ground region corners.** Inserting or deleting a corner on a ground region did nothing.

## Changes
- **Much faster contours for models that mix roads with other sources.** When a model had CRTN or CRN roads, the rest of the model (point, line and area sources, building diffraction) was calculated on a single core. It now uses every core, as other models do, with identical results. On P1987 refinement takes 52 s instead of 340 s.
- **Faster building diffraction checks.** The visibility checks behind diffraction round building sides now run in parallel, again with identical results.
- **Fewer pauses on large projects.** Autosave no longer rewrites a project that hasn't changed since its last autosave (each rewrite re-encoded every stored contour result, pausing the window for seconds on big projects). Background memory clean-up waits for a pause in your input, and a loaded project is excluded from it altogether.
- The stall log (`~/Library/Logs/AURIS/stalls.log`) now names the AURIS version, says whether AURIS was in front, marks pauses caused by macOS (App Nap, sleep) rather than AURIS, and records how long each pause lasted.

## New features
- **Difference sheets by drag and drop.** On the Contours Result grid, drag one result tile onto another (for example Proposed onto Existing) to make a difference sheet between them.
- **Receptor levels for every scenario and time slice.** The Result grid now has a table of each receptor's level per scenario and time slice, with the change from the first scenario.
- **Export every calculated result at once.** One image per result plus a single combined PDF, from Export, the File menu or Report Pack.

## Changes
- **SmartSmooth Simplify and Smoothing work together visibly.** Smoothing now rounds off the corners of the simplified shape. It used to redraw the original contour through the simplified points, so Extreme with 100% Smoothing looked unchanged. On its own, Smoothing also evens out small jagged steps in the raw trace. Every setting stays within its accuracy limit.
- **Sharper, more accurate shadow edges.** Building-corner shadows where one roof takes over from another, and side paths that switch round the other side of a group of buildings, are now traced exactly. Before, these were left as sawtooth edges. On P1998 the worst 1% of points are now within 0.22 dB of exact levels (was 0.44 dB). Calculation takes about 20% longer on such sites.
- **Interpolated draws exact bands.** Building and barrier shadow edges are now straight lines instead of staircases, and the remaining "star" artefacts around mesh points are reduced (about 15% closer to exact levels).
- **Section views trace barrier and roof shadow lines for every point source.** With more than one source, sections used to trace none.
- **Faster refinement near walls and barriers.** Refinement no longer spends its point budget on receivers exactly on a wall, and barriers now separate the field for line, area and road sources (a small area-source test model: 168 s → 107 s).
- The 3D view now explains when its renderer isn't available, instead of failing. This is preparation for a Windows build.

## Changes
- **Road (CRTN/CRN) contours are now smooth and accurate in Interpolated, Gradient and SmartSmooth.** These projects skipped the extra calculation that adds receivers along shadows and barriers, so the smooth methods could only blend the coarse grid: shadows looked pixellated with a blur, and contours scalloped along barriers. They now get it too, and every barrier is a hard edge in the field. On a test model the result matches exact CRTN calculations within 0.1 dB. Calculation takes longer with a smooth method selected (P1930 at 4 m: about 50 s to 2 minutes); Raw is unchanged.
- **The update splash is a compact liquid-glass card.** The wave artwork fills the card, a clear glass panel holds the logo, text and progress, and the progress bar keeps gliding even while AURIS is busy starting up.
- **Drawing-tool defaults are kept between sessions.** Values you set in a tool's defaults before drawing (heights, levels, building properties and so on) now survive restarting AURIS. Factory defaults are unchanged until you change them.

- Small white specks could appear in Gradient view near building corners.
- The window's rounded corners could show a dark rim, more visible when AURIS was not the active window.

## Changes
- **SmartSmooth Simplify and Smoothing now work in sequence, as two clear steps.** Simplify turns each contour into a cleaner polygon, and each step on the slider looks visibly stronger: Extreme is deliberately faceted, so long road contours become clean straight runs. The amount follows each contour's own size, so tight rings near a source and long bands far from it are simplified to the same look; small rings are no longer flattened while large bands barely change. Smoothing then rounds the corners of that simplified shape with Bézier curves. At 100% it draws true arcs through the corners, and lower settings soften them less. Before, turning Smoothing on traced the raw contour again and could make lines more detailed instead of smoother.
- **Pick from screen samples any window or app** with the macOS colour loupe. It no longer needs Screen & System Audio Recording permission or a restart.
- The status bar's "Saved / Unsaved changes" check runs after you edit, instead of every second, which keeps AURIS responsive on large projects.

## Bug fixes
- **3D view images were saved upside down.** Saved and copied 3D views were mirrored top to bottom (since 0.18.7). They now match the view on screen.
- **The splash after an update no longer freezes (beachball).** The font list used for plots was rebuilt after every update on the main thread, holding the splash for several seconds. It is now kept between updates, and when it does have to be built, the splash keeps moving.

## New features
- **Calculate every scenario and time slice in one go.** The Contours Result page now shows a grid with one tile per scenario and time slice. Teal is the result on screen, white tiles are calculated, amber means the inputs have changed since, and empty tiles are not calculated yet. Click any tile to show that result. The Calculate button's second half is now **All**: every scenario and time slice, all time slices of this scenario, all scenarios for this time slice, or all views. Hover a choice to see which tiles it covers. During the run the tiles fill as they're calculated and the grid counts down ("Calculating 3 of 4 · about 2 min left"), then AURIS returns to the result you started on. Each scenario's results are saved, so they're all there when you reopen the project.
- **Interpolated contours keep fading shadow edges sharp.** Where a building's acoustic shadow fades out partway across an area, the level step along its edge no longer blends into neighbouring grid cells: each side takes its values from its own receivers, and beyond the point where the step fades, the field joins up smoothly again. Checked against 2,500 exact calculations on P1995, the field near these edges is closer to the true levels: average error 0.12 → 0.10 dB, and 90% of points within 0.20 dB (was 0.30 dB). Elsewhere it is unchanged.

## Changes
- **The SmartSmooth curve-smoothing slider now does what it says.** At 25%, 50% and 100% the curves follow the calculated contour progressively more loosely, within the same accuracy limits. Before, all three settings drew almost the same lines.
- **Faster contour meshing.** The step that joins neighbouring cells of the contour mesh runs about twice as fast with identical results (P1995: 24 s → 12 s of contour preparation).

## Bug fixes
- **Switching scenario could mark another scenario's contours as out of date.** After calculating one scenario's Day and then another's, going back showed "Inputs have changed since this result". Each scenario now keeps its own record.
- After switching time slice, the Grid note could say the displayed contour was stale and name the previous slice.

## New features
- **Sound events per time slice (SEL).** Point, line and area sources can now be continuous, a number of discrete events, or off in each time slice. Describe one event by its sound exposure (LwE, or SEL measured at a distance; a pass-by for a line) and, optionally, its LAFmax. AURIS turns N events in the slice into the equivalent continuous level, which receptors, contours and spectra use. The Inspector shows a live readout, for example "40 events → equivalent LwA 83.4 dB over the period". Projects from earlier versions are unchanged.
- **LAFmax for line sources with pass-by events.** The maximum is placed at the line's nearest point to each receptor and propagated with the same ISO 9613-2 route. A source that is off or excluded in the active slice no longer contributes a maximum.
- **Site outline drawing:** a crosshair while drawing, a stroke-only preview, and a line-width slider (0.5–8 px) saved with the project and used on sheets and in exports.

## Changes
- **Soft elevation everywhere.** Settings, panels and switchers use one wide, soft, low-contrast shade instead of stacked hard rings.
- **Straight shadow edges in Interpolated contours.** Where a building's acoustic shadow begins, levels step by about 5 dB. Interpolated mode drew those steps as a sawtooth because many shadow lines stopped a fraction short of a building corner or a neighbouring line, so the contour blended straight across the step. These near-misses are now closed. On P1995 the share of shadow-line length that separates the field went from 50% to 77%, and the edges are drawn straight.
- **SmartSmooth fits smooth curves to each contour** instead of rounding the corners of a simplified polygon. That removes straight chords across arcs, bulges and hooks at building ends. Where a curve would break a safety check (usually a few metres beside a shadow edge or a building), only that stretch now stays close to the calculated line. Previously the whole line did, which made the 100% setting look less smooth than 25%. P1995 at 8 m: largest shift at the default settings 3.1 m → 0.5 m, and each slider change rebuilds faster (2.5 s → 1.8 s).
- **Contour refinement spends its receivers along features.** Areas the refinement could not afford in one pass stay in line for the next, and the cells beside a failed area are checked next. This gives even detail along diffraction edges instead of isolated 0.5 m patches beside untouched 8 m cells.
- **The contour progress bar follows the real work.** With buildings, most of the time goes into screening transitions, so the bar no longer races to 55% on the grid and then crawls.
- **The status-bar progress glides** like the dialog bars. Copy and Export on the contour sheet confirm with a tick (Copied / Saved) instead of a dialog, Copy Table confirms on its button, and secondary buttons show a clear hover and pressed state.

## Changes
- **Faster screening-transition checks.** AURIS no longer tests shortcut paths that would have to pass through a building. A P1995 contour at 2 m went from 384 s to 226 s, with exactly the same contours.

## Bug fixes
- **Contours could fail with "Contour band merge failed to preserve classified faces"** on some sites (P1995 at 2 m). When neighbouring contour faces met at almost the same corner, the geometry library could drop a whole face while joining a band. AURIS now retries the join on a 1 nm grid and, if needed, adds back any face that was lost, then checks that every face is kept before using the result.

## Bug fixes
- **Crash:** building the Contours panel could crash AURIS. PySide can fail while creating fading effects, and the panel made dozens of them; its rows now open and close without them.
- **Contours could fail with "not a valid face cover"** on some sites (P1986 and P1988). Two meshing defects are fixed: a zero-area spike on a contour face made a valid triangle look uncovered, and a face whose boundary touched itself lost pieces when it was clipped to the grid.
- **Calculation worker:** the packaged app rebuilt Matplotlib's font cache in every process. Calculations sat at 0 % for around 13 seconds, and Update Grid could fail with "Matplotlib is building the font cache". The cache is now kept between runs and built once, in the background, after you install or update.

- **Dual-carriageway roads** were not drawn in the editor for projects opened from a file (since 0.18).
- Opening an older project could show a "Contour presentation failed" dialog when its SmartSmooth result needed more receivers. AURIS now shows the calculated grid and asks for Update Grid. Results from an earlier version say so, instead of "Inputs have changed".
- The scenario picker could be too narrow or too wide, or run past the window edge and hide its arrow.
- Quitting AURIS with the 3D view open could crash as it closed.
- *Clear all* in the site outlines panel looked clickable when there was nothing to clear.

## Changes
- **Smoother, more accurate contours.** SmartSmooth and the interpolated raster now read a bounded cubic field instead of straight-sided triangles. Against known exact fields this is 3 to 10 times more accurate, grid-scale kinks fall from 5 to 12 degrees to about 2, there is no overshoot, and calculated nodes are kept exactly. Shadow boundaries behind buildings stay sharp.
- **Native CRTN contours are about 7 times faster** (P1930 at 4 m: 313 s to 46 s). The paragraph 11 ground check now uses the slope of the terrain the propagation paths actually cross, instead of the steepest slope anywhere on the site. Levels move by 0.03 dB on average and at most 0.10 dB, because roads are split into fewer segments that still meet the 2 dB rule. Dense transects show no new steps.
- Screening-transition validation does less repeated work for the same result (identical contours on P1995).
- **Settings:** the second tab is now called *Global*. It holds settings for every project on this Mac; the Project tab holds settings saved with the open project.
- The Studio sheet look has a 22 mm logo, and a bordered contour scale lines up with the cards above it. The footer date fits on one line.
- Parking areas no longer draw a large P on the map; the key still shows it.
- The Results *More* menu, the Inputs report menu and the section right-click menu use the app's menu style.
